points: Changing a big table in place can lock it or rewrite every row, so online migrations build the new shape beside the old one and switch over with a brief lock.
Expand and contract adds first and removes last, so old and new code both keep working at every step and any step can be paused or undone.
Buildkite widened an integer key by adding a bigint column, writing both, backfilling in batches and swapping, where an in-place change needed days to weeks of downtime.
GitHub queues its migrations and runs one ALTER at a time per cluster through gh-ost, because concurrent migrations compete for resources and run longer.
Shopify says sharding with Vitess turned migrations from weeks into hours, at the cost of added complexity for developers.
